chunks: Prepare against them whatever force and cavalry you can muster, that you may strike terror thereby in the enemies of God and your own, and others besides them whom you do not know but God knows. And whatever you spend in the way of God will be paid back to you in full, and no wrong will be done to you.

key_terms.رِّبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ: Cavalry or stationing of horses for border defense
key_terms.يُوفَ إِلَيْكُمْ: Will be paid back to you in full

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'preparing force' and 'ribat al-khayl' for jihad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as establishing the comprehensive nature of 'strength' (quwwah), encompassing not only physical military power but also economic, intellectual, and spiritual capabilities required for deterrence. The mention of 'ribat' (garrisoning) highlights the continuous state of readiness and vigilance necessary to protect the community against both known adversaries and hidden foes, such as internal traitors or external powers. This assurance of full recompense for expenditures underscores the principle that material sacrifices in the path of God are never wasted, reinforcing the link between worldly preparation and divine reward.
